page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture, this server features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, resulting in 2 threads per core. It is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include bundled local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores fall into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show an average read and write speed of 44.77 GB/sec and 35.36 GB/sec respectively for large uncached blocks, though small-block cached read bandwidth is weak at 253.84 GB/sec. Multi-threaded operations, such as bzip3 decompression, register poor performance in the bottom 10%, while single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and text processing maintain average throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2d-standard-4 offers dedicated AMD EPYC resources at a standard general-purpose density, making it a predictable option for workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or high-performance multi-threaded execution. Tradeoffs include limited multi-core scaling and lower database operation performance. This instance is best suited for general-purpose workloads, single-threaded applications, basic web serving, and lightweight text processing tasks that benefit from dedicated CPU allocation without demanding high memory bandwidth or parallel processing power.
